items.title: 'A cell, a bed, a toilet': Andrew's birthday in a police lock-up
items.description: Ostracised by his family and stripped of his titles, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor celebrates his 66th birthday with police.

items.title: Police consider investigation into Pauline Hanson comments
items.description: Senator Pauline Hanson has accused the government of trying to put her "back in jail" after police said they were considering an investigation over her inflammatory comments about Muslims during a media interview.

items.title: Antarctica faces 'devastating changes' under high emissions future
items.description: Scientists say parts of Antarctica face "devastating" and "irreversible" impacts from climate change unless urgent action is taken to limit greenhouse gas emissions.

items.title: Eric Dane, star of Grey's Anatomy and Euphoria, dies aged 53
items.description: The star was best known for his role as Dr Mark Sloan in long-running medical drama Grey's Anatomy, and as the patriarch of the Jacobs family in teen hit Euphoria.

items.title: Residents urged to evacuate as bushfire rages in central-east Victoria
items.description: Residents in a remote Victorian community have been urged to evacuate as an out-of-control  fire rages nearby.

items.title: Live: Wheatley set for Olympic debut as women's ski cross begins
items.description: Australia's only ski cross athlete, Kyra Wheatley, makes her Winter Olympics debut tonight as seeding begins in the women's event. Follow live.

items.title: No refunds for participants as Rottnest Channel Swim cancelled
items.description: Perth's iconic Rottnest Channel Swim has been cancelled as forecast strong winds and unfavourable ocean conditions leaves thousands of swimmers and support crew disappointed.

items.title: Eleven Australian 'ISIS brides' are trying to come home. This is who they are
items.description: The ABC can reveal the names of the 11 women connected to former Islamic State fighters in Syria who attempted to journey home to Australia this week.

items.title: NSW man caught with 34,000 'depraved' child abuse images avoids jail
items.description: A man has avoided time behind bars and instead been handed a three-year community corrections order for possessing 34,000 child abuse images and more than a dozen bestiality videos.

items.title: Menacing letters sent to politicians bear hallmarks of Sydney mosque threats
items.description: The ABC can reveal two of the threatening, hate-filled letters sent to Lakemba Mosque this month bear close resemblance to similar racist letters sent to multiple politicians since 2022.

items.title: The Orwellian twist in Trump's first Board of Peace meeting
items.description: Unless the Board of Peace begins to focus and genuinely tries to make the world a better place, this may well prove to be yet another monument to Donald Trump.

items.title: A blow to Trump could be a $1.4b windfall for Australian businesses
items.description: Modelling by consulting firm EY Australia shows Australian exporters would be owed more than $1.4 billion in refunds collectively if the US tariffs are struck down.

items.title: Coroner identifies missed opportunities in teen’s allergic reaction death
items.description: A Victorian coroner hands down her findings into the death of a teenager who suffered a severe allergic reaction to a delivery meal — but it's unclear if more urgent treatment would have saved his life.

items.title: Mercedes F1 boss calls out 'total bulls**t' as engine saga goes to vote
items.description: Toto Wolff accuses rival Formula 1 manufacturers of ganging up on Mercedes to pressure the governing FIA to change engine rules, but says it will make no difference.

items.title: Man accused of performing Nazi salute at AFL explores mental health defence
items.description: Tylere Baker-Pearce, 39, was initially charged with giving the salute at the Gabba, and was later hit with two additional counts of the alleged offence.

items.title: What to watch, read and listen to this weekend
items.description: From a cursed vagina to a classic retold, there's plenty of culture to dig into this weekend.

items.title: Licence for antibiotic use in Tasmanian salmon may be suspended
items.description: The federal agency that approved the use of an antibiotic for Tasmania's salmon industry has proposed to suspend that licence, in the wake of news the antibiotic has been found in native species.

items.title: Safety concerns at forefront as MotoGP moves to Adelaide street circuit
items.description: A rider, a reporter and a road safety expert say it will be difficult to make it safe for motorcycles to race around the Adelaide Parklands.

items.title: Perry's evolution cements greatness as milestone looms
items.description: Cricket superstar Ellyse Perry will become the first woman to play 350 matches for Australia across all formats on Saturday.

items.title: Amyl frontwoman Amy Taylor goes from tiny bikini to big legal battle
items.description: What began as a photo shoot with champagne, ice cream and humorous glamour shots of Amy Taylor, singer from punk band Amyl and the Sniffers, has escalated into a legal fight over copyright, the US Constitution and an application for a restraining order.

items.title: Toddlers' blood lead levels at 10-year high in smelter city of Port Pirie
items.description: The percentage of two-year-old children above the blood lead level threshold in Port Pirie is the highest in a decade, according to the latest figures.

items.title: 'This is ridiculous': Sport concussions spur inventor to design helmet
items.description: A lot of research has gone in to treating concussions, but now scientists are testing a new helmet to see if it can prevent them before they happen.

items.title: Pacific countries to use Tuvalu's plight as example to world powers
items.description: Fiji, Palau and Tuvalu look set to host world leaders and climate change ministers in the lead-up to COP31 in a bid to encourage larger countries to accelerate cuts to emissions.

items.title: Nurses' strike cancelled after pay rise before state election period begins
items.description: The Australian Nursing and Midwifery Federation cancels a strike at one of Adelaide's largest public hospitals after securing a 2 per cent pay rise on top of a 4 per cent immediate increase in wages announced earlier this week.

items.title: Bikie guilty of hiring sniper to gun down rival at Perth motorplex
items.description: Bikie David Pye is convicted of murder after he paid a trained sniper to assassinate his former friend and ex-Rebels boss Nick Martin in front of horrified onlookers at a drag racing event.
